generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A system with multiple valid context sources or multiple semantically distinct identity fields can pass happy-path tests while selecting the default source or relabeling one field as another across an adapter boundary.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Select the first/default context object because the actor is authenticated, then reuse a convenient generic code field for a more specific downstream identity field.
trigger_signals: adapter maps fields with similar names
code and version are both present in the canonical model
generalized_learning.reusable_control: Create deliberately divergent source identities and semantic field values, then assert owner selection and field meaning at every producer/adapter/persistence boundary.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Model role ownership and semantic identity fields explicitly; never infer a specialized identity from a generic code or from the current actor when an owning reference exists.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: For every multi-source or multi-identity adapter, execute a divergent fixture where all candidate identifiers differ and verify the canonical source at each boundary.

transfer_cases.procedure: Use two simultaneous profile states and a delegated beneficiary; verify the owner-specific state is selected.
Use distinct generic-code, product-code and version-code values; verify no downstream field is relabeled or dropped.

skill_changes.description: Persist a generic source-selection/semantic-identity prevention pattern for future delivery cycles.
Require divergent multi-source and semantic-field controls during future saturation.
